Answer: B
Reason: Figure 3a (chest X-ray) shows a visible azygos fissure in the right upper lung field, but the characteristic teardrop-shaped opacity of the azygos vein at its inferior end is absent. This "empty" appearance of the fissure is a known radiographic sign following pneumothorax and reexpansion, where the vein may be displaced or compressed, distinguishing it from the normal finding described in option A.
